keyVerseText: And God is able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work:
rootMeaning: The root of αὐτάρκεια (autárkeia) is αὐτάρκης (autárkēs), which conveys the idea of being content or self-complacent. This etymology highlights a state of self-sufficiency or independence, suggesting not merely a passive contentment but an active competence and sufficiency that comes from within. Unlike the English glosses of 'contentment' or 'sufficiency,' the root emphasizes an intrinsic completeness or adequacy that does not rely on external circumstances.
usageInScripture: The term αὐτάρκεια appears only twice in Scripture, reflecting a consistent but nuanced usage. It is translated once as 'sufficiency' in 2 Corinthians 9:8, emphasizing God's provision that enables believers to abound in good works. The other occurrence is rendered as 'contentment' in 1 Timothy 6:6, highlighting an inward state of satisfaction. This duality in translation reveals the word’s range from an external competence or adequacy to an internal, spiritual contentedness.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding αὐτάρκεια as both self-sufficiency and contentment enriches the Christian grasp of reliance on God. It reminds believers that true sufficiency is found not in worldly resources but in God’s grace, which empowers and satisfies. This word challenges the believer to cultivate a heart of contentment that is independent of fluctuating circumstances, rooted in the sufficiency of Christ’s provision. It underscores the gospel truth that spiritual competence and peace come from God alone, fostering a faith that trusts in His sustaining grace rather than in self-reliance.
keyVerseReflection: 2 Corinthians 9:8 declares that God is able to make all grace abound so that believers may always have 'all sufficiency' in every circumstance. The use of αὐτάρκεια here conveys that this sufficiency is comprehensive and reliable, enabling Christians to abound in every good work. This sufficiency is not merely material but spiritual, reflecting God’s empowering grace that meets every need and equips believers for faithful service.
